tldr: Headlines across 22 countries assert that Iran and Oman are in the final stages of a Strait of Hormuz shipping agreement, while US military threats and tanker explosions underscore the deal's fragility — producing a split narrative of imminent diplomacy and continued armed standoff.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to render Trump's threat in direct colloquial speech ('gonna be open very soon, or Iran is gonna get hit') — uniquely prioritising the visceral threat-register over the diplomatic framing every other outlet chose.

Only headline to cast Iraq itself as an active party ('Iraq in talks with Iran to facilitate vessel transit') — every other bucket frames the deal as Iran-Oman bilateral, making the Iraqi actor invisible.

Only headline to emphasise the physical scale of disruption ('Hundreds of ships remain stranded') rather than the diplomatic arc — an ECONOMIC/CAPACITY angle absent from all other buckets' lead headlines.
Only headline devoted entirely to the tanker explosions incident as a standalone story ('Vessel reports hearing two blasts in Hormuz Strait') rather than subordinating it to the deal narrative.

bottom_line: The headline layer frames the Strait of Hormuz story as an imminent Iran-Oman shipping deal, but wraps it in a US military threat backdrop and contested claims about who is really negotiating — leaving readers with simultaneous signals of breakthrough and continued standoff.
